technology-science.title: Technology & science
technology-science.standfirst: In this section: The CIRUS research reactor; TIFRAC, India's first home-built computer; IIT Kanpur; Bhilai Steel Plant.

items.title: The CIRUS research reactor
items.summary: CIRUS, a 40 MW research reactor at Trombay near Bombay supplied by Canada, first went critical in July 1960. It ran on natural uranium with heavy water supplied by the United States.

items.title: TIFRAC, India's first home-built computer
items.summary: The Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Automatic Calculator, based on the IAS machine design, was formally commissioned and named by Nehru in 1960 and stayed in use until 1965.

items.title: IIT Kanpur
items.summary: IIT Kanpur began in December 1959 on the campus of the Harcourt Butler Technological Institute and was established by an Act of Parliament in 1960.

items.title: Bhilai Steel Plant
items.summary: The Bhilai Steel Plant, set up with Soviet help from 1955, became India's main producer of steel rails.

government-politics.title: Government & politics
government-politics.standfirst: In this section: President: Rajendra Prasad; Prime Minister: Jawaharlal Nehru; The second Lok Sabha; Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960.

items.title: President: Rajendra Prasad
items.summary: Rajendra Prasad was President of India, in office from 1950 to 1962.

items.title: Prime Minister: Jawaharlal Nehru
items.summary: Jawaharlal Nehru was Prime Minister, with Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan as Vice-President and B. P. Sinha as Chief Justice.

items.title: The second Lok Sabha
items.summary: In the 1957 election, for 494 of the 505 Lok Sabha seats, the Indian National Congress won 371.

items.title: Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960
items.summary: The Act divided Bombay State into Maharashtra and Gujarat, which came into being on 1 May 1960.

items.title: The Border Roads Organisation
items.summary: The Border Roads Organisation was formed on 7 May 1960 to secure India's borders and develop roads in remote northern and north-eastern areas; its first projects were raised that May.

items.title: The Ninth Amendment
items.summary: The Constitution (Ninth Amendment), in force from 28 December 1960, made minor adjustments to the territory of the Union after an agreement with Pakistan to settle disputes by demarcating border villages.

sources.label: Wikipedia: Ninth Amendment of the Constitution of India

children.label: Lok Sabha
children.role: Lower house: 494 of 505 seats were elected in 1957, 371 won by Congress

steps.detail: The States Reorganisation Act drew states on linguistic lines but left a bilingual Bombay State of Marathi, Gujarati, Kutchi and Konkani speakers.

steps.label: Agitation
steps.detail: The Samyukta Maharashtra Samiti campaigned for a Marathi-speaking state.
The Bombay Reorganisation Act split Bombay State, and Maharashtra came into being on 1 May 1960.

freedom-history.title: Independence & history
freedom-history.standfirst: In this section: Maharashtra and Gujarat are born; Nehru and Zhou Enlai agree to talks; The Second Five-Year Plan.

items.title: Maharashtra and Gujarat are born
items.summary: On 1 May 1960 the state of Maharashtra was formed from the division of Bombay State, after the Samyukta Maharashtra movement.

items.title: Nehru and Zhou Enlai agree to talks
items.summary: In 1960 Nehru and Zhou Enlai agreed that officials of both countries would examine the historical basis of the boundary dispute; the sides disagreed on the western sector.

items.title: The Second Five-Year Plan
items.summary: The Second Plan, 1956 to 1961, focused on the public sector and rapid industrialisation, following the Mahalanobis model; steel plants contracted during the First Plan came into production.

items.title: The Nanavati case
items.summary: The Bombay High Court overturned a jury's not-guilty verdict on 11 March 1960 in the trial of Commander K. M. Nanavati for shooting his wife's lover, and sentenced him to life; the case drew unprecedented press coverage and the Supreme Court upheld it on 24 November 1961.

personalities.title: Famous personalities
personalities.standfirst: In this section: Jawaharlal Nehru; Rajendra Prasad; Milkha Singh; Satyajit Ray; K. Asif.

items.title: Jawaharlal Nehru
items.summary: Prime Minister, born in Allahabad in 1889.
items.whyThisYear: He agreed with Zhou Enlai to hold official-level talks on the boundary and named TIFRAC.

items.title: Milkha Singh
items.summary: Sprinter, born in 1929.
items.whyThisYear: He finished fourth in the 400 metres at the Rome Olympics.

items.title: Satyajit Ray
items.summary: Film-maker, born in Calcutta in 1921.
items.whyThisYear: His film Devi, with Sharmila Tagore, was released in 1960.

items.title: K. Asif
items.summary: Director, born in 1922.
items.whyThisYear: Mughal-e-Azam, which he produced and directed, was released on 5 August 1960; its development began in 1944.

items.title: Dilip Kumar
items.summary: Actor, born in 1922.
items.whyThisYear: He played Prince Salim in Mughal-e-Azam.

items.title: Madhubala
items.summary: Actress, born in 1933.

items.title: Homi J. Bhabha
items.summary: Physicist, born in Bombay in 1909.
items.whyThisYear: The CIRUS reactor at his Trombay establishment went critical in July 1960.

items.title: Lata Mangeshkar
items.summary: Playback singer whose voice carried Hindi film songs for decades, later one of the most recorded artists in history.
items.whyThisYear: She sang 'Pyar Kiya To Darna Kya' for Madhubala in Mughal-e-Azam (composed by Naushad), and 'Ajeeb Dastaan Hai Yeh' and 'O Sajna' for 1960 films.

achievements.standfirst: In this section: Olympic hockey silver; A record-breaking film; India's second nuclear reactor.

items.title: Olympic hockey silver
items.summary: India's only medal at Rome was silver in hockey, ending a run of six Olympic golds from 1928.

items.title: A record-breaking film
items.summary: Mughal-e-Azam became the highest-grossing Indian film to that time, a distinction it held for 15 years.

items.title: India's second nuclear reactor
items.summary: CIRUS, the second nuclear reactor built in India, first went critical in July 1960.

items.title: Hockey final: Pakistan 1, India 0
items.summary: Pakistan won the gold on 9 September 1960 with a sixth-minute goal by Ahmed Naseer Bunda. India had won 30 straight Olympic matches before this one.

items.summary: Milkha Singh finished fourth in the Olympic 400 metres final in 45.6 seconds, behind Otis Davis, Carl Kaufmann and Malcolm Spence.

steps.text: India beat Australia 1-0 after extra time, Bhola scoring in the 84th minute.
